description:
Found by the HexDocs cold test (defk-djy.9, docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy.md, point 5). A first-draft kernel wrapped its body in a for used as a value (for-collect). The compiler reported that, plus byte_size/1, and stopped: the map, Map.update, |>, Enum.reduce and :math.log2 inside the for's body were only reported after the for was rewritten, costing a round trip. A newcomer expects every error in one run.

Today the compiler does not look inside a rejected construct (language.md section 11 and getting-started 'Reading a compile error' now say so, defk-djy.9). Option: when a for (or another construct) is rejected for its shape, still lower its body in a recovery mode that collects the body's own rejections while suppressing errors that only follow from the rejected construct (types of the for's value, etc.). Risk: cascades and misleading follow-ups; the existing 'without the errors an earlier one causes' rule must hold.

Done when the attempt1 kernel in docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy/attempt1.ex.txt reports for-collect, unknown-function (byte_size), unsupported-map, unsupported-call (Map.update/Map.values/Enum.reduce/:math.log2) and pipe in one compile, with no cascade errors, a compile_errors_test case covers it, and the sentence in language.md 11 and getting-started is updated.

comments.text:
> *This was generated by AI during triage.*

## Agent Brief

**Category:** enhancement
**Summary:** When a `for` is rejected for its shape (for-collect), the compiler still reports the errors in its body in the same compile, without cascade errors

**Current behavior:**
The compiler does not look inside a rejected construct. The HexDocs cold test's first attempt (docs/cold-tests/hexdocs-entropy/attempt1.ex.txt) reports for-collect and byte_size, then stops; the map, Map.update, |>, Enum.reduce and :math.log2 inside the for's body appear only after the for is rewritten. docs/language.md (section on compile errors) and getting-started ("Reading a compile error") say errors inside a rejected construct appear only after it is fixed.

**Desired behavior:**
- A `for` rejected for its shape (for-collect, and other shape-only rejections of `for` if they share the path) still has its generators, filters and body checked in a recovery mode that collects their own errors.
- Errors that only follow from the rejection (the type of the for's value, uses of a binding it would have produced, missing accumulator) are not reported. The existing rule that the compiler reports errors "without the errors an earlier one causes" must keep holding; when in doubt, suppress.
- Other rejected constructs are unchanged.

**Key interfaces:**
- Compile error collection in the compiler, and the `for-collect` entry in `Defk.Errors`
- docs/language.md and getting-started sentences about errors inside rejected constructs

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] compile_errors_test: attempt1 reports, in one compile, for-collect, unknown-function (byte_size), unsupported-map, unsupported-call for Map.update/Map.values/Enum.reduce/:math.log2 and pipe, and no other errors
- [ ] A for-collect whose body is valid reports only for-collect (no cascade)
- [ ] Existing compile_errors tests and the compile-errors doc test pass unchanged (apart from intended additions)
- [ ] The docs sentences are updated; `mix test`, `mix docs`, `mix credo --strict` clean

**Out of scope:**
- Recovery inside other rejected constructs (if/cond/case shapes, unsupported calls with block arguments)
- Changing which constructs are rejected

title: Report compile errors inside a construct the compiler rejected
